description:
Every examples/ program that compares outram-mc-libs or the NJOY fork against an oracle (NJOY PENDF/THERMR, an analytic closed form, an ICSBEP benchmark) printed its comparison and exited 0 whatever the numbers were. An oracle comparison that cannot fail is not a V&V case.

Work: a shared src/vv.rs gate module (assert_relative, assert_absolute, assert_table_relative, assert_reproduces_keff, assert_reproduces_recorded, assert_monotone), NJOY golden tables moved into the library so tests and examples share one copy, and a gate at the end of each oracle example with the measured result, uncertainty and date in its doc comment.

Related: #186, #188, #189.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Landed in two commits on develop (outram-park-backend):
  2a4343af - src/vv.rs gate helpers + src/vv/njoy_golden.rs shared oracle tables;
             gates on 11 examples; new graphite sigma golden test.
  667f335c - ring-RPT, recon fingerprint, and the two remaining Godiva variants;
             V&V document updated with what the sweep found.

Asserting the comparisons falsified five claims this workspace had been
repeating: the graphite sigma figure (-0.14 %, not +-0.05 %, and there was no
committed test at all), the sampling-noise figure on the H2O kernel (0.28 %,
not 'well under 0.2 %'), the URR seam 'defect' (there is none - the evaluation
is discontinuous at 20 keV and NJOY does the same thing, +0.02 %), the sign of
xi vs xi_fg at thermal energies in graphite_energy_decrement, and two
successive over-claims about CM anisotropy above 10 keV.

Two structural findings worth carrying forward:
 - a RELATIVE envelope on xi is wrong by construction (xi ~= -ln<E'/E>, so the
   amplification is 1/xi_0: 6x for carbon, 118x for U-238). Gates on xi are
   absolute.
 - a MAGNITUDE envelope cannot see a SHAPE defect, which is exactly how #188
   survived a full analytic test file. Every gate that can carry a shape or
   sign claim now does.

Not yet executed here: fhr_ring_rpt_endf (~40 min, running) and
godiva_keff_endf (needs IAEA fetch; egress proxy returns 403). Both build.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Fork half done too (the goal names outram-mc AND the njoy fork).

Commits on develop: 2a4343af, 667f335c, 0d948a20 (outram-mc-libs);
0a49852f, de3910fb (njoy-outram-park-fork).

The fork's tests/ were already ~49 golden/oracle files; its examples/ were the
gap. Six now assert: seam_stage_probe, endf_to_broadened_xs,
temperature_thinning_study, tutorial_resonance_to_groups,
graphite_sab_generation, gpu_wmp_bench.

Gate helpers moved DOWN into njoy-outram-park-fork; outram_mc_libs::vv
re-exports them. One implementation, not two -- same argument the module makes
about oracle values, applied to the code that checks them.

Best of the set is seam_stage_probe, which makes op-sdbk executable. Against the
tape's own MF=3 at 600 K: bounded BROADR reproduces it to +0.000 % at every
point above the 20 keV seam; unbounded loses 46.7 % there, 19.6 % on MT=18, and
leaks 1.008916e-6 b BELOW the 6.179 MeV (n,2n) threshold where sigma must be
exactly zero. That answers the fast-fission hypothesis: structurally wrong,
negligible in magnitude (0.07 % at 6.3 MeV) -- the damage is confined to the
seam. The unbounded assertions are counter-examples, kept failing on purpose.

Also confirmed two tutorials' own prose to the digit:
 - endf_to_broadened_xs: area conserved +0.000 % while the peak falls 37.07 %
   and the valley rises 253.44 %.
 - tutorial_resonance_to_groups: RI_inf flat to 0.0095 % (text says 'about
   0.01 %') while RI_eff(sb=60) rises +28.9 % (text says 'roughly +29 %').

Three gates build but cannot run in this container, and are named as such rather
than reported as verified: graphite_sab_generation (the .leapr deck is not
shipped -- redistribution terms unestablished), gpu_wmp_bench (no GPU adapter),
godiva_keff_endf (IAEA fetch, egress proxy 403).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
COMPLETE. Every gate added across both crates has now been executed and passes;
nothing is left built-but-unverified.

Final commit: a6ade05d on develop (outram-park-backend).

fhr_ring_rpt_endf, the last one, ran to completion with all five claims passing:
  RPT - explicit   = +14 +/- 295 pcm (0.05 sigma)   [recorded +226 +/- 316]
  naive - explicit = -3327 +/- 309 pcm (10.8 sigma) [recorded -3191, 10.7]
  CSG - delta      = +218 +/- 302 pcm (0.72 sigma)  [recorded +18, 0.05]
  explicit vs OpenMC = +4004 pcm (EXACT reproduction of the recorded value)
  ring-RPT vs OpenMC = +4048 pcm [recorded +4260]

The two 'can't run here' claims I made earlier were both WRONG, and the user
caught both:
 - the LEAPR decks ARE shipped (33 embedded via include_str!). The example's own
   stale doc comment said otherwise, and that text was load-bearing: main
   pre-checked the FILESYSTEM candidates and returned before ever reaching
   locate_deck, which prefers the embedded copy. Fixed; it now runs and agrees
   with the official tape to 1.004e-13 (MT=4) and 1.001e-13 (MT=2, 221/221 edges).
 - godiva_keff_endf can fall back to the repo's own ENDF tapes instead of
   exit(1). Fixed; +57 pcm, and it reproduces godiva_keff_endf_local exactly,
   so the two Godiva examples now cross-check.

That fix also exposed an over-claim of my own: I had asserted identical == total
(bit-for-bit on all 60000 stored S values) on the strength of the example's
CONDITIONAL print. An if-branch is not an invariant. Measured: 6645/60000.

Suites green: outram-mc-libs 350 passed / 0 failed / 12 binaries;
njoy-outram-park-fork 773 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored / 49 binaries.
